[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"ONNX Export and Inference Optimization in PyTorch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open standard format for representing machine learning models. Exporting PyTorch models to ONNX enables running them efficiently across diverse hardware platforms and runtimes like ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, and OpenVINO."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensure you have PyTorch and ONNX installed in your environment. You can install the necessary packages using pip."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install torch torchvision onnx onnxruntime"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Exporting a PyTorch Model to ONNX"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To export a PyTorch model, you need an instantiated model and a dummy input tensor matching the expected input dimensions. The torch.onnx.export function traces the execution graph and serializes it to the specified file path."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torchvision.models as models

# Initialize a pretrained ResNet18 model
model = models.resnet18(pretrained=True)
model.eval()

# Create a dummy input with the appropriate batch size and shape
dummy_input = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)

# Export the model
torch.onnx.export(
    model,
    dummy_input,
    "resnet18.onnx",
    export_params=True,
    opset_version=14,
    do_constant_folding=True,
    input_names=["input"],
    output_names=["output"],
    dynamic_axes={"input": {0: "batch_size"}, "output": {0: "batch_size"}}
)"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"export_params: Includes trained model parameters in the exported file."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"opset_version: Specifies the ONNX version to use (version 14 or higher is recommended for modern operators)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"do_constant_folding: Optimizes the graph by pre-computing constant expressions."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"dynamic_axes: Allows variable batch sizes during inference."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Validating the ONNX Model"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before running inference, it is good practice to check the structural integrity of the exported ONNX file using the built-in validator."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"import onnx

# Load the ONNX model
onnx_model = onnx.load("resnet18.onnx")

# Check that the IR is well-formed
onnx.checker.check_model(onnx_model)
print("Model validated successfully!")"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Running Inference with ONNX Runtime"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"ONNX Runtime provides high-performance execution for ONNX models. You can initialize an InferenceSession and pass numpy arrays to generate predictions."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np
import onnxruntime as ort

# Create an inference session
ort_session = ort.InferenceSession("resnet18.onnx", providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])

# Prepare numpy input
numpy_input = np.randn(1, 3, 224, 224).astype(np.float32)

# Run inference
ort_inputs = {ort_session.get_inputs()[0].name: numpy_input}
ort_outs = ort_session.run(None, ort_inputs)

print("Inference output shape:", ort_outs[0].shape)"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Advanced Inference Optimization"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can further optimize ONNX models for production by enabling graph optimizations such as operator fusion and mixed-precision quantization using ONNX Runtime configuration options."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"options = ort.SessionOptions()
options.graph_optimization_level = ort.GraphOptimizationLevel.ORT_ENABLE_ALL
options.optimized_model_filepath = "resnet18_optimized.onnx"

# Re-initialize session with optimization enabled
optimized_session = ort.InferenceSession("resnet18.onnx", options, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
print("Model optimized and saved successfully!")"}]
